passage: Thursday night. Over dinner Kunal said, "So... are we ever having a baby?" and I nearly dropped my spoon. For two years I assumed we both meant "later". I never asked because it felt awkward, like touching something that might break. Turns out Kunal has been thinking of next year, and I have been thinking of five years from now, when the promotion has settled. We talked until the dal went cold. Kunal is worried about waiting too long and I am worried about money and time, and neither of us knew the other was carrying it. I wish we had spoken before it piled up. Relieved it's out, and a bit foolish. Going to set a time to talk properly on Sunday, with tea. - Bhupen

(Nirmala and Vikas, married two years, texting from separate rooms one night.)
Nirmala: can I ask something I've been avoiding
Vikas: ok that's ominous
Nirmala: when do you actually want kids
Vikas: honestly? I thought we'd start this year. I assumed you did too
Nirmala: this year?? I was thinking in 3 or 4 years. after my PhD
Vikas: why didn't you say
Nirmala: why didn't YOU say. every time your mom hinted, we both just changed the subject
Vikas: I thought it was obvious
Nirmala: nothing about this is obvious. I'm also scared about my body, my career, money
Vikas: I didn't know any of that
Vikas: I'm scared too. that I'm getting older and we're drifting
Nirmala: we should have talked two years ago
Vikas: yeah. can we sit down tomorrow, properly? in person
Nirmala: yes. I don't want to do this over text

passage:
In their village outside Karnal, everyone asked Preeti and Chetan the same question at every wedding and funeral: "Any good news?"
They would both smile and change the subject. At home, they never spoke about it either. Chetan assumed Preeti wanted to wait, like him. Preeti assumed Chetan wanted a child soon, like his mother kept saying.
Two years passed like that.
One evening, walking back from the fields, Preeti finally said it. "I want to finish my nursing course before a baby. At least two more years."
Chetan stopped on the path. "I also want to wait. The dairy loan isn't cleared yet."
They stared at each other. Then Preeti laughed, and cried a little.
"And I'm afraid," she said. "My sister nearly died in childbirth."
Chetan hadn't known she carried that fear. Two years of silence, and now all of it at once.

qa.q: What course does Preeti want to finish?
What was Preeti feeling when she laughed and cried a little?
qa.a: Preeti felt relieved that they both wanted to wait, but also anxious and emotional, carrying a fear from her sister's childbirth.

qa.q: What else could Preeti and Chetan have done instead of changing the subject for two years?
qa.a: They could have talked privately early on about their plans and fears, so they didn't carry separate assumptions.

qa.q: How might Chetan feel learning of Preeti's fear?
qa.a: Chetan is likely surprised and sad, realising she carried a big fear alone for two years.

grounding: It shows a couple avoiding the topic and assuming the other agreed, then learning after two years that their timelines and worries were different.
